newsitem.title: USA: Sony considers IPO for entertainment unit.
newsitem.headline: Sony considers IPO for entertainment unit.

text.p: Sony Corp president Nobuyuki Idei said Tuesday the company has no plans to sell its entertainment division but would consider an initial public offering sometime in the future.
"We have no intention to sell (Sony Pictures Entertainment or SPE)," Idei told reporters at a briefing here. "I think SPE is and will be a very important part of our business."
Idei reiterated Sony would consider selling a stake of SPE to the public but he cautioned the company would need "an appropriate amount of preparation" before such a deal could be announced.

Idei said the company recently hired First Boston as a financial consultant, but he said the move did not mean Sony was nearing a decision on a stock offering, adding the company has relationships with a number of Wall Street investment banks, including J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley and Bear Stearns.
"I don't deny my intention is to make the company public when we've had an approrpriarte time of prerparation,' he said.
Idei declined to say how long it would take before Sony made a decision or how much of the entertainment company Sony would offer to shareholders.
Sony's entertainment division includes Sony Pictures, the umbrella company for Columbia Pictures and TriStar Pictures, Sony Music and Sony Theaters.

During a wide-ranging meeting with reporters to introduce Sony Pictures Entertainment's new management team, Idei said the company is committed to expanding the entertainment portion of the company's business, which currently accounts for about 20 percent of Sony's revenues.
Sony purchased Columbia Pictures in 1989 for $3.4 billion. Since then it has struggled to find the right management team to provide a steady stream of box office hits.
